root_idea.summary: The root centers on something entering into, penetrating, or becoming fixed within something else.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop meanings of inward burning or thirst, water running among trees, a hidden object, rancor lodged in the breast, concealed appropriation, restraints encircling the limbs, and transmission through intervening places.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Form I verb has Quran-attested senses of dishonest appropriation and shackling or figurative withholding.
The QAC group contains the homographic nouns غُلّ and غِلّ, both Quran-attested and retained as distinct numbered senses under one transparent public headword.
The Quran-only feminine form is normalized to the passive-participle citation form مَغْلُول.

senses.definition: To act unfaithfully in taking from communal spoil or booty; to embezzle or defraud.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of secretly appropriating something that should remain in the division of spoil; Quranic occurrences are in the construction of acting unfaithfully in relation to booty.

senses.definition: To shackle, bind, or confine with a neck or hand fetter.
senses.usage_conditions: The passive may describe someone whose hand or limbs have been shackled; the imperative may command that a person be shackled.

senses.definition: To withhold a hand from expenditure, figuratively treating it as shackled.
senses.usage_conditions: A metaphorical construction describing restricted generosity or refusal to spend; it is distinct from the physical act of fastening a fetter.

senses.definition: A shackle, fetter, or iron collar for the neck or hand.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural أَغْلَال is used for shackles and fetters; the Quranic imagery includes restraints placed around the neck.

senses.definition: A burdensome restraint, difficult obligation, or fatiguing task, figuratively likened to a shackle.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative Quranic use of أَغْلَال; it should not be reduced to the physical implement alone.

senses.definition: Rancor, malice, enmity, spite, or concealed ill will.
senses.usage_conditions: غِلّ denotes hostility or resentment lodged in the breast, including resentment that is removed from the hearts of the people of Paradise.

senses.definition: Shackled, bound, or constrained as by a fetter.
senses.usage_conditions: The form is a passive participle of the act of fastening a غُلّ and may describe a hand or person as bound.

senses.definition: Withheld from spending; figuratively tight-fisted or restricted in giving.
senses.usage_conditions: Used metaphorically of a hand whose giving is restrained, especially in the Quranic image of a hand bound to the neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something enter into another thing, or to enter into it; to penetrate or become intermingled with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive and intransitive uses are attested, including entry into a thing or into the midst of deserts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional transitive use, recorded independently from the meanings of entering and concealing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause oil or perfume to penetrate among the roots of the hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with hair, the head, or perfume introduced beneath or among the hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To conceal or make something unapparent to someone without that person's knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction used of hiding an object or matter from another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For water to run or enter amid trees and their gaps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes water moving through wooded interspaces rather than an ordinary open current.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on or wear a garment beneath other garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is explained through entering into the garment; it concerns layered clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thirsty, severely thirsty, or inwardly burning from thirst, anger, or vexation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person and, in related usage, of an animal that has not fully satisfied its thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the breast or heart to become affected with rancor, malice, spite, or insincerity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the vocalized verb construction with the breast as subject, not simply the noun غِلّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a she-camel a mixture of date stones and fodder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized feeding expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain silent about a matter, or to be intent upon it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same construction is reported with these two related contextual applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perfume someone or smear perfume abundantly into the beard; also to perfume oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II intensifies the application or causes perfume to be introduced into the beard or moustache.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give camels or other livestock insufficient water, leaving them thirsty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV construction describes incomplete satisfaction of thirst and may be used of livestock that remain thirsty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For land or an estate to yield revenue, or for someone to bring its proceeds to a household.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the onset, production, delivery, or collection of غَلّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a valley to produce or support the growth of plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is the vegetation known as غُلّان or related growth in a valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave some flesh or fat adhering to the hide during skinning; likewise, to leave milk remaining in an udder during milking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized sense of incomplete extraction, attested in butchering and milking contexts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an orator or preacher to say what is incorrect or improper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied specifically to faulty speech or delivery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look intensely or intently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the eye or sight in a construction of concentrated looking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An overt hostile or predatory incursion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use of the Form IV verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of clothing oneself with or wearing a coat of mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized military-clothing use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drink a beverage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form VIII usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a camel, sheep, or goat to become affected by the disease called غَلَل.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal-specific disease use is distinct from ordinary thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To obtain, receive, or collect revenue; or to require someone to bring revenue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of taking the yield of land or estates and, figuratively, of reaping profit or advantage from someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To convey a message or letter from one place to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The message is described as passing through intervening towns or countries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A breaking or cracking of the bone of the nose or the head of a flask or bottle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physical sense, compared with غَرْغَرَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To penetrate deeply or reach into something, including reaching deeply in looking or description.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested expression concerns penetrating observation or reaching a point beyond ordinary looking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go quickly or hasten onward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form V usage from the sense of penetrating or reaching deeply.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wife, by metonymic extension from a shackle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative and colloquial application of the noun; it is not a Quranic sense of the noun group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman of bad disposition, figuratively called a foul or lice-infested shackle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression based on the traditional form of a shackle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thirst, intense thirst, or burning in the interior from thirst, anger, or vexation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun is distinct in vocalization and lexical identity from غِلّ meaning rancor and غُلّ meaning a shackle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Proceeds, revenue, or income from land, rent, crops, milk, livestock, labor, or similar productive sources.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may include agricultural yield, rent, a master's payment from a slave, and other recurring returns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clipped or rejected coins circulating in private trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical monetary use, distinct from proceeds or income.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing or place in which a person hides himself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal sense related to concealment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water running or appearing weakly among trees or in the gaps of a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe a feeble, intermittent flow that disappears and reappears at the surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strainer or clarifying cloth fitted over the mouth of a ewer or flask.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized household object; the plural may refer to such filters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flesh left on the thumb or remaining during the skinning of an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical butchering sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease affecting sheep or goats in the teat, associated with milk left unexpressed in the udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-disease term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food or drink that an old man takes into his stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression praising such food or drink.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The burning of love, grief, or inward emotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of inward burning; it is distinct from the physical mixture also called غَلِيل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Date stones mixed with fodder or dough for feeding a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-feed noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment worn next to the body beneath other clothing, or beneath a coat of mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also denote an inner lining or covering associated with armor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of cloth used beneath a woman's waist-wrapper to make the buttocks appear larger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An item of dress and adornment, distinct from the ordinary undergarment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pin joining the two ends of a coat-of-mail ring, or an inner covering associated with mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized armor-making sense and related plural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thirsty or burning-thirsty, especially of a camel that has not fully satisfied its thirst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal adjective with plural forms used of thirsty camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Low or depressed ground, a valley, or a torrent-bed containing trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural غُلّان may denote such wooded depressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant, also associated in plural with غُلّان.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical use reported separately from the geographical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion broken from the seashore and collected in one place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional or dialectal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree root extending deeply into the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a root whose penetration into the soil is emphasized.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quick rate or pace of going.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal expression for speed of travel, related but not identical in form to the verb تَغَلْغَلَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clamour and confusion of voices.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sound-related noun, distinct from the quick pace homonym.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who clings to rancor, malice, or spite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial description of persistent inward hostility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unfaithful or dishonest person, especially one unfaithful regarding a loan, deposit, or entrusted property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is distinct from the person who bears rancor and from a person involved with revenue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garden or estate that has or yields revenue and produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective or substantivized description of productive land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thirsty or affected by burning thirst, including an inward burning caused by anger or vexation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A non-Quranic lexical use of the passive-participle form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yearning or longing for someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed tropical use of the Form VIII participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A message or letter conveyed from town to town or from country to country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective describes transmission through successive places or communities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hastening or moving quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine active-participial adjective used in the sense of speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place, tract of land, or estate from which revenue is obtained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized Form X passive participle referring to a productive source of income.

cautions: The nominal QAC group combines the homographs غُلّ ‘shackle’ and غِلّ ‘rancor’; they are presented together only because QAC supplies them as one form group, with distinct senses and vocalized headword components.

Lane’s Quran citation for مَغْلُولٌ is reported with historical citation notation; the modern verse association is used here only where independently secured by QAC and is not reconstructed from the Lane notation.
The broader Classical meanings include several rare, technical, idiomatic, or dialectal uses and should not be inferred as Quranic meanings merely from root relationship.
